result.title: Not All Challenges Are Equal: Evaluating Interactive Liveness Detection Against Real-Time Face Swaps
result.summary: Remote identity verification assumes that a camera stream shows a live person, yet public real-time face-swap tools can replace that person before the stream reaches the verifier. Passive deepfake detectors generalize poorly to new generators, while interactive challenges are often selected without evidence of which gestures expose current attacks. We evaluate randomized gesture challenges in 108 live sessions with six subjects, 24 impersonated identities, and two face-swap tools, DeepFaceLive and FaceFusion, injected through a virtual camera. The static calibration segment reaches a session-level AUC of 0.878 with a frozen UCF spatial detector, while the mean across the active-gesture windows reaches 0.988. Pose and combined gestures have the highest point estimates, whereas expressions show no clear improvement. Hand occlusion against FaceFusion, configured with an occlusion mask, scores below the static baseline. The end-to-end time required to satisfy the validator also distinguishes attacks from genuine sessions, achieving a session-level AUC of 0.732, although this signal includes synthesis and transport delays. These results show that challenge sets should be tested against current attack configurations and that response time can provide an additional, deployment-specific signal.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 108 个实时会话（6 名被试、24 个被冒充身份、DeepFaceLive 与 FaceFusion 两款换脸工具经虚拟摄像头注入）中评估随机手势挑战，比较静态标定段与各主动手势窗口的检测 AUC，并考察端到端响应时间这一信号。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「哪些手势真正暴露攻击」接近 LVR 关注的视觉证据筛选与证据信息价值问题，响应时间区分攻击与真实会话也可能对推理中的停止决策或动态计算信号提供类比线索，但属较远领域，需核查是否有可迁移之处。
